readout_other: Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) for pain; Visual Analog Mood Scale (VAMS) yielding Global Affect and Global Vigor; vital signs (heart rate, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, oxygen saturation)
direction_notes: TUS produced a significant improvement in Global Affect (mood) at 10 and 40 min versus placebo, a marginal reduction in pain (NRS) at 40 min, higher oxygen saturation at 10 min, and blunted the blood-pressure reduction seen with placebo at 10 min; Global Vigor and other vital signs were not significantly different.
safety_notes: One subject experienced exacerbation of a headache following TUS which quickly subsided without sequelae and was included in the analysis; there were no other untoward effects during or after treatment or in follow-up phone interviews up to 4 months later.

exposures.label: 8 MHz diagnostic TUS to posterior frontal scalp/cortex

target.label: posterior frontal scalp overlying frontal-temporal cortex (site 5, near the temporal window)

timing.protocol_description: A diagnostic B-mode ultrasound machine (GE LOGIQe, 12L-RS probe) was applied with gel to the scalp, contralateral to the site of maximal pain, for 15 s per exposure, with settings of power 100%, depth 3.5 cm, harmonics on, cross-Xbeam on. Acoustic output values were MI 0.7, TIs 0.5, TIc 0.2 and a maximum acoustic output (AO) of 152 mW/cm2, well below FDA diagnostic ultrasound limits (MI 1.9, 720 mW/cm2).

source_quotes.n_subjects: Thirty one outpatients in the Chronic Pain Clinic at University of Arizona Medical Center South Campus were approached for this study, met criteria, and were enrolled.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Subjects received either TUS or placebo, and then the alternative.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: These include (with our chosen settings) power (100%), frequency (8 MHz), depth (3.5 cm), harmonics (on), cross-Xbeam (on), mode (B), and duration of exposure (15 s).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: These include (with our chosen settings) power (100%), frequency (8 MHz), depth (3.5 cm), harmonics (on), cross-Xbeam (on), mode (B), and duration of exposure (15 s).
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: The global maximum acoustic output (AO) was 152 mW/cm<sup>2</sup>, about 20% of the recommended limit of 720 mW per centimeter, and about 30% of Tyler’s stated safety limit of 500 mW/cm<sup>2</sup> [21].
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: exposure to either subthermal TUS (8 MHz) or placebo (in a double blind crossover study) using the 12L-RS probe of a LOGIQe ultrasound imaging machine (General Electric, USA).
source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: exposure to either subthermal TUS (8 MHz) or placebo (in a double blind crossover study) using the 12L-RS probe of a LOGIQe ultrasound imaging machine (General Electric, USA).

flags.reason: Not stated as an explicit number of TUS sessions; inferred as 1 from the crossover design in which each subject received one TUS exposure and one placebo exposure.

Paper reports a console-derived 'acoustic output (AO)' value of 152 mW/cm2 compared against the 720 mW/cm2 FDA ISPTA limit, suggesting it represents ISPTA, but the paper never explicitly names it as ISPTA or states whether it is a free-field or derated in-situ value; placed in unspecified_domain.
Device is a standard diagnostic B-mode imaging probe; no pulse duration, PRF or duty cycle for the imaging pulse sequence is disclosed, so waveform could not be classified.

Paper reports that a spectrum analyzer detected a faint 12.8 kHz signal from the probe during TUS but judged it inaudible to subjects and staff, and subjects reported detecting no sound; this is a post hoc inaudibility check rather than an active masking method, coded as 'other'.
